## Why

This is a learning project, and the point is to see how the agent works. The browser chat (#52) shows only the user's messages and the coordinator's replies, plus "Working: update_trip_brief…" while a tool runs. Everything in between is hidden: what the model thought, which tools it called with what input, what each tool sent back, and how long the turn took. The terminal chat shows some of it, but Joe wants to use the browser. This issue adds a raw view to the browser chat that shows the whole loop of each turn.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 4.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.1.

Decided when the issue was written, and in the struck-out open questions below:

- **The chat is a list of cards, like other chat apps.** The user's messages are cards on the right. The coordinator's replies are cards on the left.
- **A "Raw" toggle on the chat view adds more cards on the left.** Off, the chat shows only the user's messages and the coordinator's replies. On, the left side also shows the cards listed under Do: the turn's start, the message the model got, thinking, tool calls, tool replies, other system messages, and the turn's end, in the order they happened. The right side doesn't change. There's no second column.
- **The raw cards aren't saved.** They live in the browser tab's memory only. A reload, or opening a session again, shows the conversation with no raw cards. The transcript is not changed.
- **The tab keeps the raw cards whether the toggle is on or off.** So turning it on partway through a session shows them for the turns already sent from this tab.
- **The coordinator's thinking is shown as a summary.** The coordinator already thinks: adaptive thinking is the Agent SDK's default for its model. But the thinking text comes back empty. The saved transcripts hold thinking blocks with only a signature, the encrypted form the API needs to go on with the conversation. The SDK's `thinking: { type: "adaptive", display: "summarized" }` returns a summary of the thinking in those blocks. It changes only what's returned, not how much the model thinks or what it costs.

## Open questions

- ~~What each item in the details column looks like: readable cards like the terminal chat, or each Agent SDK message as raw JSON?~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: readable cards, laid out as above. Thinking in italics, a tool call as its name and input, a tool reply in a box. Long tool inputs and replies are cut to about 15 lines, with a "show all" to open the rest.
- ~~Who sees the toggle: every user, or only Joe?~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: every user. The cards hold only the user's own trip data, plus the model's name and the tool names.

## Do

- Turn on summarized thinking in the coordinator's options (`src/agent/coordinator.ts`), and add a line about it to the technical spec.
- Pass these to the browser, in order, for each turn the tab sends (`src/agent/turn-event.ts`, `src/api/turn-stream.ts`). Each becomes a raw card on the left:
  - The turn's start: the model and the tools it was given.
  - The message the model got, with the app's lines added, such as the date and the resumed line (technical spec 5.2). It goes on the left, since the app wrote those lines, not the user.
  - Each thinking summary, reply text, tool call with its full input, and tool reply with its full text and whether it was an error.
  - Any other system message from the SDK, such as a retry, as its subtype and data.
  - The turn's end: how long it took, the number of model calls, input and output tokens, and why it failed, if it did.
- Show the conversation as cards, and add the "Raw" toggle and the raw cards to the chat view (`web/src/chat-page.tsx`, `web/src/chat-state.ts`).

## Done when

- A test with a fake turn (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) shows each kind of item above reaching the browser's stream.
- On the deployed site after the merge (systems design, section 7), Joe turns on "Raw", sends a message that makes the coordinator call a tool, and sees on the left, in order: the start, the message with the app's lines, a thinking summary, the tool call with its input, the tool's reply, the reply text, and the end with its time and tokens.
- With "Raw" off, only the user's messages show on the right and the coordinator's replies on the left.
- After a reload, the conversation is restored as cards, with no raw cards.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

## Why

This is a learning project, and the point is to see how the agent works. The browser chat (#52) shows only the user's messages and the coordinator's replies, plus "Working: update_trip_brief…" while a tool runs. Everything in between is hidden: what the model thought, which tools it called with what input, what each tool sent back, and how long the turn took. The terminal chat shows some of it, but Joe wants to use the browser. This issue adds a details view to the browser chat that shows the whole loop of each turn, without mixing it into the conversation.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 4.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.1.

Decided when the issue was written:

- **A toggle, "Show details", on the chat view.** Off, the chat looks as it does now. On, the view splits into two columns: the conversation on the left, and the details on the right. Each column scrolls on its own.
- **The details aren't saved.** They live in the browser tab's memory only. A reload, or opening a session again, starts the details column empty. The transcript is not changed.
- **The tab keeps the details whether the toggle is on or off.** So turning it on partway through a session shows the turns already sent from this tab.
- **Each turn in the details column starts with the user's message,** so it lines up with the conversation on the left.
- **The coordinator's thinking is shown as a summary.** Today the coordinator's options set no `thinking`, so the model's thinking comes back empty. The Agent SDK's `thinking: { type: "adaptive", display: "summarized" }` returns a summary of it. This changes only what's returned, not how the model thinks.

## Open questions

- What each item in the details column looks like. One way is readable cards, like the terminal chat: thinking in italics, a tool call as its name and input, a tool reply in a box. The other way is each Agent SDK message as raw JSON, with a short header such as `assistant: tool_use update_trip_brief`. Proposal: readable cards, with long tool inputs and replies cut to about 15 lines and a "show all" to open the rest.
- Who sees the toggle: every user, or only Joe? The details hold only the user's own trip data, plus the model's name and the tool names. Proposal: every user, since it's less code and nothing in it is secret.

## Do

- Turn on summarized thinking in the coordinator's options (`src/agent/coordinator.ts`), and add a line about it to the technical spec.
- Pass these to the browser, in order, for each turn the tab sends (`src/agent/turn-event.ts`, `src/api/turn-stream.ts`):
  - The turn's start: the model and the tools it was given.
  - The message the model got, with the app's lines added, such as the date and the resumed line (technical spec 5.2).
  - Each thinking summary, reply text, tool call with its full input, and tool reply with its full text and whether it was an error.
  - Any other system message from the SDK, such as a retry, as its subtype and data.
  - The turn's end: how long it took, the number of model calls, input and output tokens, and why it failed, if it did.
- Add the toggle and the details column to the chat view (`web/src/chat-page.tsx`, `web/src/chat-state.ts`).

## Done when

- A test with a fake turn (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) shows each kind of item above reaching the browser's stream.
- On the deployed site after the merge (systems design, section 7), Joe turns on "Show details", sends a message that makes the coordinator call a tool, and sees, in order: the start, the message with the app's lines, a thinking summary, the tool call with its input, the tool's reply, the reply text, and the end with its time and tokens.
- Turning the toggle off shows the chat as it was before this issue.
- After a reload, the details column is empty, and the conversation is restored as before.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
